description: Agent installation companion to SETUP.md: background bot, on-demand tmux CLI, shared conversation verification, and everyday start/stop handoff.
agent_rules: Never print TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, or any value marked secret, into the transcript, a log, or a diff.
Never edit a start script to add a Node or Codex path; use the documented environment overrides.
Never widen CODEX_SANDBOX_MODE to unblock a failing command without asking the human first.
Ask the human to run `codex login` themselves; it opens a browser.
Default delivery includes background system services and an on-demand tmux entry to the same app-server; a first Telegram reply alone is not completion.
Reuse existing configuration and check service/command ownership before installing. Do not launch a duplicate worker for the same token.

probes.fail: Native Windows is unsupported. Use WSL2.
Checkout is on a Windows drive mount. DrvFs does not enforce the socket permission bits that are this system's only access control, and breaks SQLite WAL. Move to the Linux filesystem.
Install Node >= 22, or set TELECODEX_NODE_BIN. Do not edit scripts.
npm is needed by telecodex.setup.sh and by the Codex pin.
Install tmux on the bot host using its native package manager; use it for the CLI frontend, not as a substitute for bot service supervision.

probes.degrades_to: Block-LaTeX images are skipped; text delivery is unaffected. Two tests in test/latex-renderer.test.ts do fail without it.
Socket liveness uses a Node connect probe instead; Codex Desktop relay detection (macOS only) stays off.

secrets_from_human.obtain: The human messages @BotFather on Telegram with /newbot and pastes the token back.
secrets_from_human.blast_radius: Holding this token allows access to bot updates and posting as the bot. Keep it out of transcripts, logs and commits.

secrets_from_human.obtain: Numeric Telegram user ids, comma separated. The human gets theirs from @userinfobot. Usernames are not accepted.
secrets_from_human.blast_radius: This list is the only authentication in the system. Everyone on it can do anything Codex can do on this host. Confirm every digit with the human.

env.advice: The only meaningful containment in the system. Do not widen it to unblock a command.
Only never is supported. Other values are rejected at startup; approval interaction must be implemented in a fork.
app-server is the shared-writer architecture the start scripts and TELECODEX.md describe.
Lowercase. Also the profiles/<botKey>/ directory name and the worker argument.
all-authorized is not a bypass; it runs after the allowlist check.
Set in .telecodex.env when automatic Node resolution picks the wrong interpreter. Configuration loads before runtime discovery.
Set in .telecodex.env to use an existing Codex CLI. Setup, service scripts and direct CLI wrappers all read this file.
Only for API-key auth. The default is the host's existing `codex login` session.

steps.then: Fill only missing credentials; preserve existing configuration. Do not echo secrets. Default BOT_KEY is main.
Write profiles/main/profile.json with the human-selected absolute default_workspace. Use the same workspace for the desktop CLI entry; do not assume the source checkout is the work directory.

steps.on_failure: Have the human complete ./telecodex-bin/codex login, or use login --device-auth on a headless host.

steps.then: Check ownership, execute the rendered installation commands, start app-server/Core/worker in order, and verify actual running services. Linux uses systemd user units (linger for logout survival); macOS uses launchd agents. Do not leave three foreground terminals as the installed result.

Follow SETUP.md section 6 to configure a tele-kei shortcut using native tmux and telecodex-remote. Create/reattach one CLI session, use switch-client when already in tmux, pass the chosen workspace and resume --all, and share the bot app-server. Ensure telegram-active is on the service and CLI PATH.

Verify a real Telegram reply, a real CLI turn followed by Telegram continuing that same content and thread, tmux detach/reattach, bot replies while detached, and controlled service stop/start. Record checks not performed; do not claim a machine reboot test without one.

Give the bot link, workspace, desktop entry, detach shortcut, worker-only pause/resume versus full-stack shutdown/restart commands (including the effect on CLI), reboot/login behavior and one log location. Keep the human handoff short.

verify.when: Development changes or diagnosis require it; normal installation does not need a full development test run.
Development changes or diagnosis require it; normal installation does not need a full development test run.
